body.v: ParcelPoint: your parcel is being held. To have it delivered, pay the CHF 1.99 fee within 24 hours.
After this deadline, the parcel will be returned to the sender.

hotspots.explain: parcelpoint-fees.example is not ParcelPoint's domain, which is parcelpoint.example.
"within 24 hours" is there to rush you. And with a fee this small, paying seems risk-free.
The page would ask for your card details. A real carrier does not make you pay fees through a link in a message.
The threat of the parcel being sent back comes on top of the deadline.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone borrowing ParcelPoint's name. The address is on parcelpoint-fees.example, not parcelpoint.example. The text-message versions pull exactly the same trick.
choices: Someone with an almost identical address

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Haste, with a touch of worry: pay within 24 hours or the parcel goes back.
choices: Hurry: pay within 24 hours or lose the parcel
The wish to receive a free gift
None, it is just a delivery notice

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Pay a small fee through a link. Your card details would go to the sender.
choices: Pay a small fee through a link
Collect the parcel from a neighbour

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not take the route they offer you. Check the delivery in the carrier's app or website, opened by you. A click "just to look" can already be enough, and replying STOP confirms that your address is active.
choices: Open the ParcelPoint app yourself and check
Pay anyway, it is only CHF 1.99
Reply STOP to be taken off the list

actions.label: Ignore the link and check the delivery yourself in the ParcelPoint app
actions.consequence: No parcel is on hold. The email was fake.

actions.label: Pay anyway, it is only CHF 1.99
actions.consequence: Your card details go to the scammer, who can now charge far more than CHF 1.99.

actions.label: Click the link just to look, without entering anything
actions.consequence: A quick look can confirm your address is active, and some pages try to run code behind your back.

actions.label: Reply STOP to be taken off the list
actions.consequence: Your reply proves the address is real. You will get more of them.

attacker_reveal: Old recipe, new packaging: a tiny fee, a short deadline and a ready-made link. Come in through the door you already know, the app, and I have nothing left to sell you.
